ranked.headline: Learned latent representations for single-cell and spatial transcriptomic inference
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications extend deep latent models to multimodal, spatial, and cross-platform transcriptomic datasets with a transferability emphasis.

ranked.headline: Conditioned generative models steer biomolecule design toward explicit property targets
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair diffusion, RL, and LLM agents with physics tools to target enzyme activity, binding, and PTM sites.

ranked.headline: Single-cell dynamics inferred from live imaging, morphology, splicing and gene networks
ranked.summary: Recent single-cell studies couple time-resolved imaging, morphology, splicing kinetics and regulatory networks to models of cell fate dynamics.

ranked.headline: Benchmarking simulators against real Nanopore error profiles and structured repeats
ranked.summary: Simulated Nanopore reads still miss the full real error profile, motivating tools for repeats and transmission inference.

ranked.headline: Coupled dynamical modules guide pattern formation and inference in biological models
ranked.summary: Preprints now couple simulation and likelihood-based inference to mechanistic models of cortical, cellular, and Physarum dynamics.

ranked.headline: Pangenome assemblies resolve LINE-1, NUMT, and de novo mutation variation in humans
ranked.summary: Long-read pangenome assemblies and sibling-based designs now resolve mutation, retrotransposon, and mitochondrial insertion variation at population scale.

ranked.headline: Deep models condition molecular design and activity prediction on biological context
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and one publication embed transcriptomic state, structural confidence, and gene-level activity into deep models.

ranked.headline: Software linking variant data to curated knowledge and learned pathogenicity predictors
ranked.summary: Fragmented gene panel resources and variant pathogenicity scoring call for tools that combine curated data with learned predictors across disease domains.

ranked.headline: LLM agents and typed knowledge structures are being constrained for biomedical analysis
ranked.summary: Biomedical LLM agents are now being evaluated on process and reproducibility, not only final answers, as structured retrieval addresses known failure modes.

ranked.headline: Computational inference of methylation and genome features validated against references
ranked.summary: Read-level and single-cell sequencing now support inference of methylation, readthrough and lncRNA features, with benchmarks against independent truth.

ranked.headline: Automated tools and benchmarks for quantifying spatial and morphological cell data
ranked.summary: Open pipelines and annotated benchmarks are emerging for reproducible quantification of cytology, volume EM, and spatial transcriptomics data.

ranked.headline: Computational frameworks for benchmarking single-cell and multi-omics analysis pipelines
ranked.summary: New tools and benchmarks test omics pipelines for stability, regional bias, confounding, and cross-platform integration in public datasets.

ranked.headline: Transport and interpretable models infer biological dynamics from snapshot data
ranked.summary: Unpaired, incomplete, and single-snapshot biological datasets motivate dynamical models with explicit transport or interpretable structure.

ranked.headline: Pretrained protein and DNA models adapted for PTM, variant effect, and interpretability
ranked.summary: Pretrained ESM2 and Nucleotide Transformer encoders are being reshaped with biological structure, sparse features, and task-specific losses.

ranked.headline: Agents convert unstructured biomedical literature into structured, computable records
ranked.summary: Expert-in-the-loop agentic extraction is now applied to degradation assays, QSP models, causal graphs, and gene-disease causal evidence.

ranked.headline: Bayesian and neural inference recovers biological model parameters from noisy data
ranked.summary: Measurement artifacts, timing uncertainty, and stochastic noise are now modeled explicitly during parameter estimation rather than treated as residual error.

ranked.headline: Graph models encode biological priors for interaction and disease-association prediction
ranked.summary: Recent graph learners embed explicit biological priors across PPI, drug-target, and disease-gene prediction tasks.

ranked.headline: Discrete tokens and contrastive embeddings extend protein structure and binding design
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply lookup-free quantization, flow matching, and discrete diffusion to protein sequence-structure and ensemble tokens.

ranked.headline: Sampling and likelihood layers shape recovered conformational states in biomolecules
ranked.summary: Generative and enhanced-sampling methods now target PTM-conditioned, mechanical, and disordered protein ensembles across preprints and three published studies.

ranked.headline: Benchmark leakage and shared controls inflate single-cell perturbation prediction scores
ranked.summary: Benchmark construction now determines whether reported gains in perturbation and virtual screen prediction reflect genuine predictive capability.

ranked.headline: Inferring biomolecular graph structure with resampling, causal and Bayesian DAG methods
ranked.summary: Multi-graph and local estimands with finite-sample error control address large-scale interventional, heterogeneous, and multiomics biomolecular data.

ranked.headline: Learned models predict, generate, and personalize gut microbiome compositions
ranked.summary: Three preprints from May 2026 extend learned sequence representations to microbiome prediction, synthetic generation, and personalized diet design.

ranked.headline: Force balance and nutrient depletion drive microbial colony separation and detachment
ranked.summary: Mechanistic models now link density, adhesion and gravity-driven flow to discrete microbial outcomes like colony separation and detachment.

ranked.headline: Genome-scale metabolic models reconstruct and simulate microbial function across scales
ranked.summary: Learned protein and molecular representations are now being paired with constraint-based simulation to annotate metabolic function.

ranked.headline: Adaptive time constants, enzyme capacity and inhibitory plasticity shape system dynamics
ranked.summary: Recent preprints treat adaptation of time constants, enzyme capacity and inhibitory plasticity as determinants of system dynamics.

ranked.headline: Deep learning maps genetic variants onto missense pathogenicity and regulatory readouts
ranked.summary: Deep learning and genomic language models are moving variant interpretation toward quantitative, cell-type-resolved regulatory readouts.

ranked.headline: isomiR-resolved modeling of miRNA targeting and extracellular vesicle provenance
ranked.summary: Recent preprints treat isomiRs as separate analytical units for target prediction, read denoising, and EV source attribution.

ranked.headline: Feature-based protein predictors tested against held-out and experimental data
ranked.summary: Explicit benchmarks across enzyme, stability, kinase, and antibody tasks now show where current molecular predictors remain limited.

ranked.headline: Curated gene families link microbial enzymes to host, habitat, and substrate
ranked.summary: Curated, context-specific annotation resources now extend microbial gene family analysis to genome and metagenome scales.

ranked.headline: Computational tools select guide RNAs and editors before genome editing experiments
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published resource add sequence- and protein-aware computational design for PAM/TAM mapping, base editor screens, and editor selection.

ranked.headline: Learned models score and generate immune peptide and antibody interaction sites
ranked.summary: Protein language models are now fine-tuned for TCR specificity profiling and interaction-site prediction, moving beyond structure-only binding scores.

ranked.headline: Analysis pipeline choice shifts resistome profiles in metagenomic benchmarks
ranked.summary: Large-scale benchmarks and new viral and metatranscriptomic tools show how method design affects metagenomic inference.

ranked.headline: RNA conformational ensembles inform protein and ligand recognition modeling
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs frameshifting-element simulations, protein-RNA torsion analysis, and RNA docking benchmarks to test computational RNA models.

ranked.headline: Software workflows formalize proteomics QC and peptide-to-protein quantification
ranked.summary: Large-scale proteomics increasingly demands automated, reproducible QC and quantification logic, reflected in new open-source tools and a roll-up benchmark.

ranked.headline: MD and Markov models resolve allosteric states in TRMT2A and LRRK2 conformations
ranked.summary: Simulation-derived conformational landscapes now link residue-level determinants to allosteric transitions and inhibitor binding affinity.

ranked.headline: Multi-omics and genome resources map candidate genes in plant and fungal systems
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply RNA-seq benchmarking, interactome construction, multi-omics, and chromosome-scale assembly to plant and fungal biology.

ranked.headline: Scoring Analytical Confidence and Method Agreement in Omics Inference
ranked.summary: Analytical choices and inter-method agreement are increasingly scored as quantities rather than fixed assumptions across these preprints.

ranked.headline: Unobserved contact structure, behavior and mobility reshape epidemic model inference
ranked.summary: Work treats within-host heterogeneity, contact network structure and human mobility as explicit model components that shift inferred epidemic quantities.

ranked.headline: Open pipelines and nanopore protocols turn pathogen reads into validated genomic outputs
ranked.summary: Recent measles, Andes virus and Plasmodium falciparum studies each formalize pathogen sequencing workflows for surveillance and preparedness.

ranked.headline: Protein language model embeddings resolve residue states and ambiguous annotations
ranked.summary: Structure-aware protein representations are now applied to residue chemistry, divergent genomes, and observation-entity inference in omics.
